text:
alice: FYI starting a canary deploy for checkout-service now (change window 09:30-11:00 UTC). rolling with feature flag `checkout_v2` at 0% -> 10% initially. release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/checkout-v2 :eyes:

deploy-bot: /deploy canary checkout-service v2.4.1 initiated by @alice. allocated 2 canary instances in us-west1.

dave: ack. watching latency and error budget. if p95 latency > 200ms or 5xx rate > 0.8% in the next 10m, we hard-pin to v2.4.0 and rollback canary.
maria: adding the pin command in case: `deploy-bot pin checkout-service v2.4.0 --reason "rollback-trigger"` saved in ops runbook.

jen: quick note — we'll soft-mute the verbose debug ff for EU to avoid noise: set `eu_debug=false` under `ops/region-overrides`. dont forget to document in release notes. :memo:

deploy-bot: canary progress: 10% traffic -> healthy. observed requests/sec: 180, p95: 120ms, 5xx: 0.12%. logging tail: `checkout::auth` unusual spike cleared.

alice: good. propose ramp plan: 10% (10m) -> 30% (20m) -> 60% (30m) -> 100% (gradual, 1h). objections?
dave: +1, but add a safety hold at 60% for 15m and an automatic rollback threshold: if error delta > 0.5% vs baseline.
maria: putting a version-armor rule: if any region reports >1% error we pin traffic back to v2.4.0 for that region only. preparing the pin script now:
```
# pin for region
deploy-bot pin checkout-service v2.4.0 --region eu-west1 --reason "auto-pin-on-error"
```

jen: I'm going to post a short blurb in #customer-success about the feature toggle schedule and a link to the exact change window. will add the temporary opt-out steps for QA.
sre-bot: ALERT RULES CHECK: anomaly detectors are in place. ramp will be paused if: p95 up 30% OR 5xx up 0.5% absolute OR CPU > 85% on canary pool.

deploy-bot: ramping to 30% now. remind: ff exposed as `checkout_v2_weight`. updating:
`checkout_v2_weight: 10 -> 30`

alice: 30% stable at +12m. no regressions reported. moving to 60% with holdpoint. tagging release notes: "Canary v2.4.1 — performance fixes for session caching".
dave: i see a small increase in tail latency in eu-west1 (p95 +18ms). not critical yet but flagging. recommend we keep the 15m hold.
maria: enabling regional pin trigger at 60% hold. if eu-west1 crosses 0.9% 5xx, region will be pinned automatically and we will continue global ramp for others.

alice: ok initiating hold. also temporary override to avoid auto-rollforward for non-critical telem: `deploy-bot set-flag telemetry_suppress=true --scope canary`

jen: published release notes and change window to the customer thread. added mitigation steps for partners who need to opt out. :thumbsup:

(6m later)
sre-bot: WATCH: eu-west1 5xx rose to 1.05% in the last 2m. action: triggering regional pin.

deploy-bot: executing: `deploy-bot pin checkout-service v2.4.0 --region eu-west1 --reason "auto-pin-on-5xx"` -> SUCCESS. shifted eu-west1 traffic back to v2.4.0.

dave: good call. leaving global ramp paused. can we surface a short post-mortem note in the runbook? include stack traces and the trace id list.
maria: captured traces and saved them under /runs/1758001234/traces. adding remediation checklist: cache TTL revert, increase local session key refresh backoff.
alice: decision: keep eu-west1 pinned, continue ramp for other regions to 60% after hold. schedule a rollback to v2.4.0 global only if other regions show correlated issues.

jen: note for release notes: mark EU region as hotfix-pinned and add a note that customer-facing checkout continuity preserved.
sre-bot: REMINDER: runbook step 4 executed (auto-pin). incident severity: sev3.

deploy-bot: canary still 30% (global excluding eu-west1). next step queued: 60% global-other after 15m hold.

alice: adding a short checklist before next step: 1) confirm error deltas back below thresholds; 2) confirm CPU < 75%; 3) confirm deploy queue empty.
dave: if any unexpected regressions within next 30m — full rollback command:
```
deploy-bot rollback checkout-service --to v2.4.0 --scope global --reason "rollback on regression"
```

maria: noted. capturing final logs and will open a follow-up thread for the EU postmortem.

jen: thanks team — smooth ops. will coordinate final rollout announcement once we hit stable 100% or execute rollback. :party_parrot:
